description: Detects DNS lookups for the recovered TuxBot v3 Evolution C2 domains backing its DNS-TXT covert channel and HTTP-polling fallback.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tuxbot-v3-evolution-iot-botnet/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/16
tags:
  - attack.t1071.004
  - attack.t1568.002
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: dns
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith:
      - 'digikalas.online'
      - 'jetross.com'
      - 'cfcybernews.eu'
      - 'captcha.kanfetka.site'
      - 'c2.tuxbot.local'
  condition: selection
level: high
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(digikalas\.online|jetross\.com|cfcybernews\.eu|captcha\.kanfetka\.site|c2\.tuxbot\.local)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, RequestType, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query IN ("digikalas.online","jetross.com","cfcybernews.eu","captcha.kanfetka.site","c2.tuxbot.local") OR DNS.query="*.digikalas.online" OR DNS.query="*.tuxbot.local") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.record_type | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query IN ("digikalas.online","jetross.com","cfcybernews.eu","captcha.kanfetka.site","c2.tuxbot.local") OR DNS.query="*.digikalas.online" OR DNS.query="*.tuxbot.local") by DNS.src DNS.query DNS.record_type | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
TuxBot v3 Telnet/SSH/ADB scanner fan-out from single host AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects a single internal host initiating high-volume outbound connections to Telnet (23/2323), SSH (22), and Android Debug Bridge (5555) ports across many distinct destinations — the propagation behaviour of TuxBot's built-in scanners (1,496-pair Telnet brute-forcer plus SSH/HTTP/ADB scanners running up to 128 concurrent connections). Article-specific to the framework's scanner sub-modules. Rationale: Targets TuxBot's named scanner sub-modules (Telnet 23/2323, SSH 22, ADB 5555, HTTP 80/8080 at 128 concurrent connections) via a destination fan-out threshold rather than a single-connection match, which is the correct shape for propagation/brute-force sweeps. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tuxbot-v3-evolution-iot-botnet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/tuxbot-v3-evolution-shows-signs-of-llm.html
ATT&CKT1046 T1595.001 T1110.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Nmap/Rapid7) sweeping the subnet
  • Configuration-management/monitoring host SSH-polling the fleet
  • Network discovery tool during asset inventory
  • Ansible/Salt master reaching many nodes over 22
  • Load balancer or uptime monitor probing 80/8080 across pools
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("nmap","masscan","nessusd","zmap","ansible","salt-minion","nuclei")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the src host and initiating process — is it a sanctioned scanner subnet/host, or an IoT/embedded device that normally only speaks HTTP? Check the destination spread (internet-wide vs internal). 2) Contain: quarantine the host and block outbound 23/2323/5555 at the egress if unsanctioned; capture the offending process. 3) Hunt: pivot the src to the C2 IP/port and DNS detections (UC1/UC2) and to systemd/cron persistence (UC4) to confirm full TuxBot infection.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionFailed","ConnectionSuccess")
| where RemotePort in (23, 2323, 22, 5555, 80, 8080)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(RemoteIP), Ports = make_set(RemotePort, 10), Attempts = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| where DistinctTargets >= 50   // 50 = fan-out threshold: a single host sweeping Telnet/SSH/ADB across dozens of hosts is scanner behaviour, well above normal client egress
| order by DistinctTargets desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where DstPortNumber in (23, 2323, 22, 5555, 80, 8080)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(DstIpAddr), Ports = make_set(DstPortNumber, 10), Attempts = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname
| where DistinctTargets >= 50   // 50 = empirical scanner fan-out threshold
| order by DistinctTargets desc
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| (RemotePort=23 OR RemotePort=2323 OR RemotePort=22 OR RemotePort=5555 OR RemotePort=80 OR RemotePort=8080)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=RemoteAddressIP4, distinct=true, as=DistinctTargets))
| DistinctTargets >= 50
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` dc(All_Traffic.dest) as distinct_targets count as attempts values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (23,2323,22,5555,80,8080) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where distinct_targets >= 50 | sort - distinct_targets
| tstats summariesonly=false dc(All_Traffic.dest) as distinct_targets count as attempts values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as ports from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_port IN (23,2323,22,5555,80,8080) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where distinct_targets >= 50 | sort - distinct_targets
TuxBot v3 Linux persistence via systemd/cron/rc.local watchdog AIInstallation Medium
Hunts non-package-manager processes installing systemd services, cron entries, or rc.local hooks on Linux/IoT hosts — the triple persistence mechanism (systemd service + cron + watchdog keepalive) TuxBot uses to stay resident. Article-specific to the framework's documented persistence installer that also spawns a keepalive/watchdog process. Rationale: Anchors on TuxBot's documented triple persistence (systemd service + cron + rc.local watchdog) by flagging writes to those exact autostart paths from non-package-manager parents, with a bias toward /tmp,/dev/shm,/var/tmp droppers typical of botnet installers. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tuxbot-v3-evolution-iot-botnet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/tuxbot-v3-evolution-shows-signs-of-llm.html
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin installing/enabling a systemd unit via systemctl
  • Config management (Ansible/Puppet/Chef) deploying cron jobs or units
  • Custom in-house software installers not run through the package manager
  • Container/cloud-init bootstrap writing rc.local on first boot
  • Backup/monitoring agent registering its own systemd service
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible","puppet","chef-client","salt-minion","systemd","systemd-sysv-install")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the written unit/cron file contents and the parent process path — a service pointing at a binary in /tmp, /dev/shm, or a hidden/renamed process is high-confidence malicious. 2) Contain: disable/remove the persistence entry, kill the watchdog/keepalive process, isolate the host, and preserve the referenced binary. 3) Hunt: hash the referenced binary against the TuxBot set (UC5) and correlate the host with the C2 (UC1/UC2) and scanner (UC3) detections.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("systemctl","crontab") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("enable","--user"))
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/init.d/","/etc/rc.local")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snapd","cloud-init","unattended-upgrade")
| where AccountName != "root" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/var/tmp/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("systemctl","crontab")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/init.d/","/etc/rc.local")
| where ParentProcessName !in~ ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snapd","cloud-init")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TuxBot v3 Linux Persistence via systemd/cron/rc.local
id: d5f3e4c6-7f80-4192-ac13-3e4f50617283
description: Detects non-package-manager processes writing systemd service, cron, or rc.local persistence used by TuxBot v3 Evolution.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tuxbot-v3-evolution-iot-botnet/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/16
tags:
  - attack.t1543.002
  - attack.t1053.003
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/etc/systemd/system/'
      - '/etc/cron.d/'
      - '/etc/init.d/'
      - '/etc/rc.local'
  filter_pkg:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/dpkg'
      - '/apt'
      - '/apt-get'
      - '/yum'
      - '/dnf'
      - '/rpm'
      - '/snapd'
      - '/cloud-init'
  condition: selection and not filter_pkg
level: medium
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*"/etc/systemd/system/"* OR *"/etc/cron.d/"* OR *"/etc/init.d/"* OR *"/etc/rc.local"*) OR @process.name:(systemctl OR crontab)) -@process.executable.path:(*/dpkg OR */apt OR */apt-get OR */dnf OR */yum OR */rpm)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\/(systemctl|crontab)$/i OR regex("/etc/(systemd/system|cron\\.d|init\\.d|rc\\.local)", field=CommandLine))
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/(dpkg|apt|apt-get|yum|dnf|rpm|snapd|cloud-init)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("systemctl","crontab") OR Processes.process IN ("*/etc/systemd/system/*","*/etc/cron.d/*","*/etc/init.d/*","*/etc/rc.local*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search NOT parent_process_name IN ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snapd","cloud-init") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("systemctl","crontab") OR Processes.process IN ("*/etc/systemd/system/*","*/etc/cron.d/*","*/etc/init.d/*","*/etc/rc.local*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search NOT parent_process_name IN ("dpkg","apt","apt-get","yum","dnf","rpm","snapd","cloud-init") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
TuxBot v3 bot-agent execution by known SHA256 hash AIInstallation High
Alerts on execution or on-disk presence of any of the 20 recovered TuxBot v3 Evolution sample hashes (the cross-compiled C bot agent for ARM/MIPS/x86_64/PowerPC/RISC-V plus Go C2 components). Article-specific: these are the exact file hashes published for this framework, so a match is a direct IOC hit regardless of CPU architecture. Rationale: Direct match on the 20 published SHA256 hashes for the TuxBot v3 Evolution bot agent and C2 components; hash IOCs are architecture-independent so a single cross-compiled binary is caught on ARM/MIPS/x86_64/PowerPC/RISC-V alike. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tuxbot-v3-evolution-iot-botnet/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/tuxbot-v3-evolution-shows-signs-of-llm.html
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst detonating a recovered sample in a sanctioned lab host that reports to EDR
  • Threat-intel platform storing the sample on a research file share
  • Reverse-engineering VM with EDR enabled
  • AV quarantine copy briefly present on disk before deletion
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("malware-lab-01","re-sandbox-01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host is production (not a sanctioned analysis/RE box) and capture execution context — path, parent, user, and any child scanner/DDoS processes. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process tree and watchdog, and quarantine the binary; block associated C2 IPs/domains at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the same hashes, then pivot confirmed hosts into the C2 (UC1/UC2), scanner (UC3), and persistence (UC4) detections to scope lateral spread within the subnet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("6b7a8e0c96c2318e747f074f9a99d26738700769ac01bba692d19fc884847737","146f6010f6ee082aab13e0148d39baefa77eaba4ff65817b511b08c2092bdfd2","bd6431fb06e4689142ef597cf00382e38ae20a5393a4d9277e45a3f5b3cbcff9","a03b0d41f5ef03328150331ffa0ed970998883f7e0343d79b2d3b95330d8e7c1","eb2fa179fde2f097c18d5d700ad87d660fc238ee14cbe5477032e60856859621","a8d70d16509e227d8306be361bc37a3dc9fe34bf476f51e361e55e6d293c2b3f","0f8bcca3ed65e980da2a1f90a767b7d543be32eeea3e9338d09d4d635a497988","96b1f96efce69b3df2dea85678d60da27e3265b4a00e39e20e64b27bb985e1561","c7a36d6b8128c41f93a32413675401a10a2b5769b221bbaa8c5c309585b73ceb","246c97957651de568e61eba1abe572f0b0f960456209995d43d53a0d7cc494a1","3ec016d637e4c9cd331edd2580a229621ad638e924a4aa29ac0342e9144ace19","2f2c3551762c03da126e45dca6fc2f997c63f0f1bfc21fd0ceed680ac6f083ce","9cd5e7e3c8bad321ef6c3d47fe25b3b56e9487f703a7eeee52db4067e6bafe61","e3a5296e762e9ee16010399666441d663beeea956382e97cca032a6a5ad06811","f1efb78887bb8783d7781c07cd13b53c9c79ebe5baa81f335838d0a6e73dec7e","f324a45fcd2a9db4e542c09486c21b08bc42d6bf76fbd5f17871090361b10815","15c17dce89deccd5172285b2650de957918aa1157cde8e4633ae15dfe31f2711","71dfbb171eca4ef9d02ff630b56e5283bbef7b375d4dbe9e8c9531bef312fa8d","511d3ffb4091cbcc94571d9fb3102e8cb424c6e187d01d53ff12078d54929bda","6aa4034dc7a2858094ff4dc59af07d6fe31119591e41599bcc0f3d0b516ee734")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in~ ("6b7a8e0c96c2318e747f074f9a99d26738700769ac01bba692d19fc884847737","146f6010f6ee082aab13e0148d39baefa77eaba4ff65817b511b08c2092bdfd2","bd6431fb06e4689142ef597cf00382e38ae20a5393a4d9277e45a3f5b3cbcff9","a03b0d41f5ef03328150331ffa0ed970998883f7e0343d79b2d3b95330d8e7c1","eb2fa179fde2f097c18d5d700ad87d660fc238ee14cbe5477032e60856859621","a8d70d16509e227d8306be361bc37a3dc9fe34bf476f51e361e55e6d293c2b3f","0f8bcca3ed65e980da2a1f90a767b7d543be32eeea3e9338d09d4d635a497988","96b1f96efce69b3df2dea85678d60da27e3265b4a00e39e20e64b27bb985e1561","c7a36d6b8128c41f93a32413675401a10a2b5769b221bbaa8c5c309585b73ceb","246c97957651de568e61eba1abe572f0b0f960456209995d43d53a0d7cc494a1","3ec016d637e4c9cd331edd2580a229621ad638e924a4aa29ac0342e9144ace19","2f2c3551762c03da126e45dca6fc2f997c63f0f1bfc21fd0ceed680ac6f083ce","9cd5e7e3c8bad321ef6c3d47fe25b3b56e9487f703a7eeee52db4067e6bafe61","e3a5296e762e9ee16010399666441d663beeea956382e97cca032a6a5ad06811","f1efb78887bb8783d7781c07cd13b53c9c79ebe5baa81f335838d0a6e73dec7e","f324a45fcd2a9db4e542c09486c21b08bc42d6bf76fbd5f17871090361b10815","15c17dce89deccd5172285b2650de957918aa1157cde8e4633ae15dfe31f2711","71dfbb171eca4ef9d02ff630b56e5283bbef7b375d4dbe9e8c9531bef312fa8d","511d3ffb4091cbcc94571d9fb3102e8cb424c6e187d01d53ff12078d54929bda","6aa4034dc7a2858094ff4dc59af07d6fe31119591e41599bcc0f3d0b516ee734")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, SHA256, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("209.182.237.133", "185.10.68.127", "194.46.59.169", "45.145.185.229", "107.174.133.119", "37.32.24.195", "154.6.197.43") or RemoteUrl has_any ("digikalas.online", "jetross.com", "cfcybernews.eu", "captcha.kanfetka.site", "c2.tuxbot.local")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["209.182.237.133", "185.10.68.127", "194.46.59.169", "45.145.185.229", "107.174.133.119", "37.32.24.195", "154.6.197.43"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["digikalas.online", "jetross.com", "cfcybernews.eu", "captcha.kanfetka.site", "c2.tuxbot.local"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2013-7471", "CVE-2014-2321", "CVE-2014-8361", "CVE-2017-17215", "CVE-2017-18377", "CVE-2018-10561", "CVE-2018-10562", "CVE-2018-20062", "CVE-2020-17456", "CVE-2022-30525", "CVE-2023-39780", "CVE-2025-34037", "CVE-2026-5815", "CVE-2007-3010", "CVE-2007-5693", "CVE-2016-11021", "CVE-2020-8515", "CVE-2021-4045", "CVE-2021-25646", "CVE-2022-1388", "CVE-2022-22947", "CVE-2022-22965", "CVE-2022-44877", "CVE-2023-1389", "CVE-2025-34117")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2013-7471", "CVE-2014-2321", "CVE-2014-8361", "CVE-2017-17215", "CVE-2017-18377", "CVE-2018-10561", "CVE-2018-10562", "CVE-2018-20062", "CVE-2020-17456", "CVE-2022-30525", "CVE-2023-39780", "CVE-2025-34037", "CVE-2026-5815", "CVE-2007-3010", "CVE-2007-5693", "CVE-2016-11021", "CVE-2020-8515", "CVE-2021-4045", "CVE-2021-25646", "CVE-2022-1388", "CVE-2022-22947", "CVE-2022-22965", "CVE-2022-44877", "CVE-2023-1389", "CVE-2025-34117")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Unauthenticated access to MantisBT admin/install.php on a production host (CVE-2026-52847) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Credential-phishing form injection via reflected XSS in MantisBT install.php (CVE-2026-52881) · [LLM] Meta open-redirect injection via reflected XSS in MantisBT install.php (CVE-2026-52881) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Broad reflected HTML/XSS payload tokens in MantisBT install.php query string · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Unauthenticated access to MantisBT admin/install.php on a production host (CVE-2026-52847) AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for HTTP requests that reach /admin/install.php with a 200 response after deployment. The installer should be removed/restricted post-install; its continued reachability is both the precondition for the reflected-XSS chain and a recon signal. Rationale: Uses the exact installer path /admin/install.php named in the advisory plus a 200-status filter; the installer's reachability is the stated precondition for the whole XSS chain and the workaround is to remove /admin. Corroborated against the GitLab advisory DB entry for CVE-2026-52847. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-52847/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-52881/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcrw-4xvv-jh49
ATT&CKT1190 T1595.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin performing an in-place upgrade or fresh install of MantisBT
  • Internal vulnerability scanner (Nessus/Qualys) probing the endpoint
  • Uptime/synthetic monitoring configured to hit the app root that redirects into the installer
  • DevOps CI pipeline validating a freshly deployed MantisBT container
  • Security team running an authorized pentest against the tracker
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("10.0.0.0/8") and csUserAgent !has "Nessus" and csUserAgent !has "Qualys"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the source IP is not an authorized admin/scanner and whether the MantisBT version is <=2.28.3. Review the csUriQuery values returned for injected HTML tokens (form/meta). Step 2 (contain): Remove or ACL-restrict the /admin directory per the vendor workaround, or upgrade to 2.28.4+; block external access to /admin/install.php at the WAF/reverse proxy. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the same source IP across web logs for other admin-path probing and for follow-on requests carrying reflected-XSS payloads (see the form-injection and meta-redirect UCs).
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem endswith "/admin/install.php"
| where scStatus == 200
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Queries = make_set(csUriQuery, 20) by cIP, csUriStem, csMethod, csUserAgent, sSiteName
| order by Hits desc

Credential-phishing form injection via reflected XSS in MantisBT install.php (CVE-2026-52881) AIDelivery High
Detects HTTP requests to /admin/install.php whose query string carries injected <form>/action markup — the credential-phishing primitive the advisory calls out, enabled by the missing CSP form-action directive. The payload is reflected from user-supplied parameters via print_test_result(). Rationale: Targets the advisory's explicit 'credential-phishing form injection' primitive using the concrete injector path /admin/install.php and injected <form action=...> tokens (both raw and URL-encoded). The missing form-action CSP directive means the injected form is the actual exploitation vector, making these tokens high-fidelity. Confirmed via GitLab CVE-2026-52881 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-52881/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcrw-4xvv-jh49
ATT&CKT1598.003 T1189 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized pentester/bug-bounty tester replaying the watchTowr PoC against the tracker
  • A generic web vulnerability scanner (Burp/ZAP/Nuclei) firing XSS templates that include <form> payloads
  • A legitimate query parameter that coincidentally contains the literal string 'action=http' (e.g. a callback/return URL param)
  • WAF audit-mode traffic replaying attack corpora
Suppression filter
| where csUriQuery has_any ("<form", "%3Cform", "formaction") // require an actual form tag, not just action=http return-URL params
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Decode the csUriQuery and confirm an injected <form> with an action pointing off-host; note the target action domain as attacker credential-harvest infra. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP and the harvest domain at the WAF/proxy, and restrict/remove /admin/install.php or upgrade to MantisBT 2.28.4+. Step 3 (hunt): Search web logs for any admin sessions or credential POSTs to the identified harvest domain, and pivot on the source IP for the meta-redirect variant and installer-probe activity.

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem endswith "/admin/install.php"
| where csUriQuery has_any ("<form", "%3Cform", "formaction", "form%20action", "action=http", "action%3Dhttp", "method=post", "method%3Dpost")
| project TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csMethod, scStatus, csUserAgent, sSiteName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Meta open-redirect injection via reflected XSS in MantisBT install.php (CVE-2026-52881) AIDelivery High
Detects requests to /admin/install.php whose reflected query string contains injected <meta http-equiv=refresh> markup — the open-redirect primitive the advisory describes, also enabled by the absent CSP form-action directive. Redirects victims silently to phishing/malware. Rationale: Targets the advisory's explicit '<meta> open redirects' primitive, requiring both an injected <meta> token and a refresh/http-equiv/url= token on the exact /admin/install.php path so it fires only on the redirect-injection shape, not generic meta references. Confirmed via GitLab CVE-2026-52881 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-52881/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcrw-4xvv-jh49
ATT&CKT1598.003 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized pentester replaying the watchTowr open-redirect PoC
  • Automated scanner (Nuclei/ZAP) firing open-redirect templates containing <meta refresh>
  • A legitimate parameter carrying a 'url=http...' return address that coincidentally sits near a meta reference
  • WAF corpus replay in audit mode
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Decode csUriQuery, extract the redirect target URL from the injected <meta ... url=> and check it against threat intel. Step 2 (contain): Block the source IP and redirect-target domain at the WAF/proxy; remove/restrict /admin/install.php or upgrade to 2.28.4+. Step 3 (hunt): Look for users who subsequently connected to the redirect-target domain (proxy/DNS logs) and correlate with the same source IP's form-injection or probe activity.

| project TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csMethod, scStatus, csUserAgent, sSiteName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Broad reflected HTML/XSS payload tokens in MantisBT install.php query string AIExploitation Medium
Hunting-tier catch-all for any HTML-injection markup reflected through /admin/install.php's six unescaped print_test_result() parameters. Broader than the targeted form/meta rules — surfaces CSS-injection UI-manipulation and event-handler probing that the tighter alerting rules miss. Rationale: Ties any HTML-markup token to the specific vulnerable path /admin/install.php named in the advisory; scoping the broad angle-bracket/event-handler net to this one endpoint keeps it deployable while catching CSS-injection UI manipulation and probing the two alerting rules don't cover. The endpoint anchor is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic WAF signature. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-52847/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-vcrw-4xvv-jh49
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Automated web scanners (Burp/ZAP/Nuclei) sweeping the endpoint with XSS payloads
  • Authorized pentest of the tracker
  • A benign query parameter containing a literal '<' or 'javascript:' substring in a URL value
  • WAF/IDS test traffic replaying attack corpora against the app
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has "Nessus" and csUserAgent !has "Qualys" and csUserAgent !has "Nuclei" and csUserAgent !has "zgrab"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Group by source IP and inspect the make_set of reflected payloads to distinguish scanner noise (many varied payloads) from a targeted single-payload exploit; check MantisBT version. Step 2 (contain): If exploitation-grade payloads are present, restrict/remove /admin/install.php or upgrade to 2.28.4+ and block the source IP. Step 3 (hunt): Escalate confirmed hits into the form-injection and meta-redirect UCs, and review whether any admin credentials were entered on the affected page during the window.
W3CIISLog

| where csUriStem endswith "/admin/install.php"
| where csUriQuery has_any ("<", "%3C", "onerror", "onload", "<style", "%3Cstyle", "<script", "%3Cscript", "javascript:")
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), Payloads = make_set(csUriQuery, 25) by cIP, csUserAgent, sSiteName
| order by Hits desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc

MantisBT self-registration (signup.php) followed by SOAP replay to mantisconnect.php from same source AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the CVE-2026-47156 exploitation path: an attacker self-registers via signup.php then immediately drives the SOAP API (/api/soap/mantisconnect.php) using the auth-bypass to impersonate the administrator. Flags a single source IP that touches the self-registration page and the SOAP endpoint within a short window — the article-specific signup-to-SOAP pivot. Rationale: Uses the two concrete URIs from the attack chain — signup.php (default self-registration, $g_allow_signup=ON) and /api/soap/mantisconnect.php (the SOAP endpoint) — correlated by source IP inside 30 min. Legit SOAP integrations authenticate with pre-provisioned service accounts and never register, so signup→SOAP from one IP is high-fidelity for CVE-2026-47156. Cross-checked watchTowr credit and the MantisBT 2.28.4 advisory confirming the endpoint and default self-registration. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-47156/ • https://mantisbt.org/blog/archives/mantisbt/846 • https://mantisbt.org/blog/archives/mantisbt/852 • https://mantisbt.org/docs/master-1.3.x/en-US/Admin_Guide/html/admin.config.soap.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1550.004
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate new user self-registers and their team's SOAP integration client shares the same NAT/egress IP
  • Security scanner (Nessus/Qualys) crawling both the signup page and the SOAP WSDL from one IP
  • Internal QA/staging test harness that registers a throwaway account then exercises the SOAP API
  • Shared corporate proxy where many users egress from one IP, coincidentally overlapping signup and SOAP traffic
Suppression filter
| where NOT (uris IN ("/scanner/*")) // exclude known vuln-scanner paths; add your integration egress IPs to an allowlist lookup and filter with `| search NOT [| inputlookup mantis_soap_allowlist.csv | fields src]`
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the source IP's full request timeline; confirm the signup.php POST created a new account (correlate with MantisBT user_create audit) and that mantisconnect.php POSTs returned HTTP 200. Check the User-Agent — SOAP libraries (PHP-SOAP, python-zeep, curl) vs a browser. 2) Contain: disable the newly-registered account, rotate the administrator's cookie_string by forcing an admin password reset (invalidates MANTIS_STRING_COOKIE), and set $g_allow_signup=OFF until patched to 2.28.4. 3) Hunt: enumerate every account created since the first malicious signup and every SOAP operation from that IP; review private issues/attachments/user-account reads for data exfiltration and check for destructive ops (project/issue deletes).
let win = 30m;
let signup = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem endswith "signup.php"
    | project SignupTime=TimeGenerated, cIP;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem endswith "mantisconnect.php"
| where csMethod == "POST"
| join kind=inner signup on cIP
| where TimeGenerated between (SignupTime .. SignupTime + win)
| project SignupTime, SoapTime=TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csMethod, scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent
| order by SoapTime desc

MantisBT SOAP endpoint (mantisconnect.php) high-volume POST burst — mass data exfiltration AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the actions-on-objective phase of CVE-2026-47156 where an admin-impersonating client hammers the SOAP API to enumerate/exfiltrate all issues, attachments and user accounts across the 71 SOAP operations. Alerts on a single source IP exceeding a per-window POST threshold to /api/soap/mantisconnect.php with large aggregate response bytes. Rationale: Anchors on the exact SOAP endpoint URI and POST method; the >100-req/10-min threshold plus large scBytes captures the '71 SOAP operations / full data exfiltration' impact called out in the advisory. Distinct pivot from UC1 (volume/bytes vs signup correlation). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-47156/ • https://mantisbt.org/blog/archives/mantisbt/846
ATT&CKT1213 T1119
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A busy legitimate SOAP integration (CI bot, dashboard, mobile app) polling issues at high frequency
  • Bulk import/export migration job run by an admin via the SOAP API
  • Monitoring/synthetic health-check hitting mantisconnect.php on a tight interval
  • A misconfigured client retrying failed SOAP calls in a tight loop (check scStatus for repeated 500s)
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("10.0.0.0") // replace with a lookup of sanctioned SOAP integration IPs; `| search NOT [| inputlookup mantis_soap_allowlist.csv | fields src]` in Splunk
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source IP and whether it maps to a sanctioned integration; inspect scStatus distribution (many 200s + large scBytes = successful bulk pulls) and User-Agent. 2) Contain: block the IP at the WAF/reverse proxy, disable the account it authenticated as, and rotate the admin cookie_string; if the org is unpatched, take the SOAP API offline ($g_enable_soap_api / webserver rule) until 2.28.4 is deployed. 3) Hunt: quantify what was read — map SOAP calls to private issues, attachments and the user-account table (id/name/email); look for follow-on destructive operations and for the same IP reappearing against other public-facing apps.
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csUriStem endswith "mantisconnect.php"
| where csMethod == "POST"
| summarize ReqCount=count(), TotalBytesOut=sum(scBytes), SuccessCount=countif(scStatus==200), UserAgents=make_set(csUserAgent,10) by cIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where ReqCount > 100   // legit SOAP clients rarely exceed 100 ops / 10 min; mass enumeration blows past this
| order by ReqCount desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| eval MB_out=round(bytes_out/1024/1024,2)

| tstats summariesonly=false count sum(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out dc(Web.status) as statusVariety from datamodel=Web where Web.uri_path="*mantisconnect.php" AND Web.http_method=POST by Web.src _time span=10m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

First-seen SOAP client on MantisBT mantisconnect.php (new source, post-bypass admin activity) AIExploitation Medium
Baseline anti-join surfacing source IPs that hit /api/soap/mantisconnect.php for the first time in 30 days — the shape of an attacker abusing the CVE-2026-47156 bypass to act with administrator privileges from a source that was never a legitimate SOAP integration. Prioritises new clients returning HTTP 200 with large payloads. Rationale: SOAP integrations are stable, allow-listable source IPs; a never-before-seen IP driving mantisconnect.php POSTs is the cleanest available proxy for post-bypass privileged abuse when request bodies aren't logged. Leftanti/append baseline anti-join is a distinct pivot from UC1 (correlation) and UC2 (threshold). Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/composer/mantisbt/mantisbt/CVE-2026-47156/ • https://mantisbt.org/docs/master-1.3.x/en-US/Admin_Guide/html/admin.config.soap.html
ATT&CKT1550.004 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A newly-deployed or relocated legitimate SOAP integration (new server, new egress IP after cloud migration)
  • Occasional developer testing the SOAP API from a workstation
  • DHCP/NAT change putting an existing integration behind a different public IP
  • Vulnerability scanner probing the SOAP endpoint for the first time this month
Suppression filter
| where src NOT IN [| inputlookup mantis_soap_allowlist.csv | fields src] // maintain an allowlist of sanctioned SOAP integration source IPs to suppress known-good new-but-authorized clients
Response runbook
1) Triage: resolve the new source IP (ASN/geo/reverse DNS) and compare its User-Agent to known integrations; confirm POSTs returned 200 with non-trivial bytes. 2) Contain: if unrecognised, block at the WAF and disable any account seen authenticating from it; rotate the admin cookie_string. 3) Hunt: 30-day baseline warms this rule — during warmup, manually validate each new IP against the sanctioned-integration inventory and pivot into UC2 (volume) and UC1 (signup) for the same IP to confirm the full CVE-2026-47156 chain.
let baseline = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(1d))
    | where csUriStem endswith "mantisconnect.php"
    | distinct cIP;
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where csUriStem endswith "mantisconnect.php"
| where csMethod == "POST"
| join kind=leftanti baseline on cIP
| summarize Requests=count(), Success=countif(scStatus==200), BytesOut=sum(scBytes), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), UserAgents=make_set(csUserAgent,10) by cIP
| order by BytesOut desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web where earliest=-30d latest=-1d Web.uri_path="*mantisconnect.php" by Web.src
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval baseline=1 | fields src baseline
| append [| tstats `summariesonly` count as recentCount sum(Web.bytes_out) as recentBytes from datamodel=Web where earliest=-1d Web.uri_path="*mantisconnect.php" AND Web.http_method=POST by Web.src | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| stats sum(baseline) as baseline sum(recentCount) as recentCount sum(recentBytes) as recentBytes by src
| where (isnull(baseline) OR baseline=0) AND recentCount > 0
| sort - recentBytes
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where earliest=-30d latest=-1d Web.uri_path="*mantisconnect.php" by Web.src
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| eval baseline=1 | fields src baseline
| append [| tstats summariesonly=false count as recentCount sum(Web.bytes_out) as recentBytes from datamodel=Web where earliest=-1d Web.uri_path="*mantisconnect.php" AND Web.http_method=POST by Web.src | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| stats sum(baseline) as baseline sum(recentCount) as recentCount sum(recentBytes) as recentBytes by src

| sort - recentBytes

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |

Turning threat intelligence into decisive action with Defender Experts

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-07-15 9 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Security teams have never had more visibility, yet rarely have they felt more uncertain. Signal pours in from endpoints, identities, cloud workloads, and a sprawling mix of third-party tools. The post Turning threat intelligence into decisive action with Defender Experts appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog .

ATT&CKT1190 T1486 T1528 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents

let LookbackDays = 7d;

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write Installation High
Service install with binPath pointing to user-writeable path or LOLBin. Detects via process telemetry (sc.exe create) and registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* writes).
ATT&CKT1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
// EventID 4697 is "Service installed" — direct signal, no cmdline-regex needed.
union
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4697
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
                  Detail = strcat("ServiceName=", ServiceName, " | Image=", ServiceFileName) ),
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where Account !endswith "$"
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\sc.exe" and CommandLine has "create"
        | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account,
                  Detail = strcat("4688 sc.exe create: ", CommandLine) )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OkoBot Malware Framework Injects Seed Phrase Phishing Into Ledger and Trezor Apps

The Hacker News
2026-07-15 21 use cases 10 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A malware framework called OkoBot has been running on Windows machines since April 2025, and one of its modules is built to con hardware wallet owners out of their recovery phrase. On an infected PC, the request comes from inside the wallet's own desktop software. Sometimes it waits until you plug the device in first. The page is malicious. The app around it is the real one you installed, and

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OkoBot Malware Framework Injects Seed Phrase Phishing Into Ledger and Trezor App
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] OkoBot 'Apple Sync' scheduled task rebuilding reverse SSH tunnel for RDP · [LLM] OkoBot implant staging files (HDUtil.exe, hwid.dat, go.bat, extl.exe) dropped · [LLM] termsrv.dll tampering to enable concurrent RDP sessions · [LLM] Windows Defender notification suppression via registry write · [LLM] Hidden Chromium extension planted via Local Extension Settings (Rilide loader) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Reverse SSH tunnel to OkoBot infrastructure from user endpoint · [LLM] OkoBot C2 beacon to moonsand.store and TookPS/Volume2 infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] OkoBot RDP enablement: Remote Desktop Users add + inbound 3389 firewall rule · [LLM] SeedHunter process injection into Ledger/Trezor wallet applications · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
OkoBot 'Apple Sync' scheduled task rebuilding reverse SSH tunnel for RDP AIInstallation High
Hunts creation of a scheduled task literally named 'Apple Sync' that OkoBot's TookPS stage registers to rebuild an hourly reverse-SSH tunnel forwarding the local RDP port. The task name is a fixed, article-specific artifact. Rationale: 'Apple Sync' is a hard-coded scheduled-task name confirmed by both THN and Kaspersky's Securelist teardown; it has no legitimate Windows/Apple origin, making name-match near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/okobot-framework-targets-cryptocurrency-wallets/120660/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/okobot-malware-framework-injects-seed.html
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1572
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Third-party sync utility that a vendor coincidentally named 'Apple Sync' (rare)
  • Internal red-team emulation of this exact IOC
  • iTunes/Apple Devices helper tasks (named 'AppleSync'/'MobileDeviceService', not 'Apple Sync' with space + schtasks create)
  • Admin scripting a scheduled task with a demo name during testing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("itunes.exe","AppleMobileDeviceService.exe") and ProcessCommandLine !has "ssh")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full schtasks/Register-ScheduledTask command line and the task XML (schtasks /query /tn 'Apple Sync' /xml) — expect an hourly trigger launching ssh/plink forwarding 3389. 2) Contain: disable+delete the task, kill any ssh.exe/sshd.exe tunnels, isolate the host, and disable exposed local RDP accounts. 3) Hunt: check for %PROGRAMDATA%\HDVideo\HDUtil.exe, hwid.dat, %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\go.bat, termsrv.dll tampering, and outbound SSH to 104.243.43.16 / 104.243.32.213 / 62.210.188.209.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_all ("create","Apple Sync"))
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask" and ProcessCommandLine has "Apple Sync")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName has "schtasks.exe" or NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| where CommandLine has "Apple Sync"
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

id: 3f2a9c1e-6b4d-4a7e-8c2f-1e9d5b7a0c31

OkoBot implant staging files (HDUtil.exe, hwid.dat, go.bat, extl.exe) dropped AIInstallation Medium
Hunts on-disk drop of OkoBot's fixed staging artifacts and their MD5s: %PROGRAMDATA%\HDVideo\HDUtil.exe, %PROGRAMDATA%\hwid.dat, %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\go.bat, %PROGRAMDATA%\oko_ver and %TEMP%\extl.exe. These paths/names are unique to this framework. Rationale: File names/paths (%PROGRAMDATA%\HDVideo\HDUtil.exe, hwid.dat, .ssh\go.bat, oko_ver, extl.exe) and their MD5s are verbatim from THN and Securelist's IOC table — a name+hash match is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/okobot-framework-targets-cryptocurrency-wallets/120660/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/okobot-malware-framework-injects-seed.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Unrelated app legitimately writing a generic hwid.dat hardware-ID cache (check path — OkoBot uses %PROGRAMDATA%/%APPDATA%)
  • Developer's own go.bat in a personal .ssh folder (rare; check content)
  • Security tooling copying the samples for analysis on a sandbox host
  • Backup/EDR agent re-materializing quarantined copies
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process (InitiatingProcessFileName) and hash-match; benign hwid.dat won't sit under HDVideo alongside HDUtil.exe. 2) Contain: quarantine the files, kill the parent chain, isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot to the 'Apple Sync' task, outbound SSH to the bot IPs, termsrv.dll modification and the moonsand.store beacon on the same host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\HDVideo\" and FileName =~ "HDUtil.exe")
    or (FolderPath has @"\.ssh\" and FileName =~ "go.bat")
    or FileName =~ "hwid.dat"
    or FileName =~ "oko_ver"
    or FileName =~ "extl.exe"
    or MD5 in~ ("ac93a821617aea1f56d4bc0bef4af327","11dbc8a2bea04b15f8f68f3f01e8faf9","70fef9fd6e351f4d53cfeee8dcdfcd99","3d2b43f91f65bfbf36a9c71b6b418876","dd52f5108a176c62ad807c327734ad12","acd31c9941b6c1cabd4e45e6877b9038")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\HDVideo\" and TargetFileName =~ "HDUtil.exe")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\.ssh\" and TargetFileName =~ "go.bat")
    or TargetFileName in~ ("hwid.dat","oko_ver","extl.exe")
    or Hash in~ ("ac93a821617aea1f56d4bc0bef4af327","11dbc8a2bea04b15f8f68f3f01e8faf9","70fef9fd6e351f4d53cfeee8dcdfcd99","dd52f5108a176c62ad807c327734ad12","acd31c9941b6c1cabd4e45e6877b9038")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Hash, ActingProcessName

termsrv.dll tampering to enable concurrent RDP sessions AIInstallation High
Hunts modification/replacement of C:\Windows\System32\termsrv.dll by anything other than Windows servicing components — OkoBot swaps in a patched build that permits concurrent RDP sessions to support its hourly reverse-RDP tunnel. Rationale: termsrv.dll is a protected System32 binary normally only touched by TrustedInstaller/servicing; the article explicitly names its replacement for concurrent RDP, so a write by any other process is high-signal. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/okobot-framework-targets-cryptocurrency-wallets/120660/
ATT&CKT1112 T1543.003 T1021.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows cumulative/quality update servicing termsrv.dll (excluded via TrustedInstaller/TiWorker filter)
  • Legitimate 'RDP Wrapper' admin tool an internal team deployed for multi-session RDP
  • Third-party patch-management agent staging a hotfix
  • Antivirus restoring a quarantined original DLL
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RDPWInst.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the modifying process and compare termsrv.dll hash/signature to the OS-shipped build (sfc /verifyfile). 2) Contain: restore the original DLL, disable concurrent-session patching, isolate host, review active RDP sessions. 3) Hunt: correlate with 'Apple Sync' task, Remote Desktop Users group additions, firewall 3389 rules, and OkoBot staging files on the host.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\System32\" and FileName =~ "termsrv.dll"
| where ActionType in ("FileModified","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","poqexec.exe","msiexec.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\System32\" and TargetFileName =~ "termsrv.dll"
| where EventType in~ ("FileModified","FileCreated","FileRename")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TiWorker.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","poqexec.exe","msiexec.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

OkoBot RDP enablement: Remote Desktop Users add + inbound 3389 firewall rule AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the OkoBot 'build a desk' sequence — adding an account to the Remote Desktop Users group, opening the firewall for inbound RDP (3389), and clearing fDenyTSConnections — from user endpoints. These are the lateral-access primitives the SSH bot sets up post-injection. Rationale: The article explicitly lists 'opens the firewall for inbound RDP', 'adds an account to the Remote Desktop Users group', and concurrent-RDP enablement — each maps to a concrete net/netsh/reg command line clustered on one host. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/okobot-framework-targets-cryptocurrency-wallets/120660/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1098 T1562.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk/IT enabling RDP + adding a support account for legitimate remote assistance
  • GPO/Intune remediation script opening 3389 on managed hosts
  • Server-build automation setting fDenyTSConnections=0
  • Pentest/red-team RDP enablement
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("IntuneManagementExtension.exe","gpscript.exe","omadmclient.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: check whether all three primitives (group add + firewall + fDenyTS) cluster on one endpoint in a short window and whether the initiating process is a known admin tool. 2) Contain: revert firewall rule, remove the added RDP account, re-set fDenyTSConnections=1, isolate if unexplained. 3) Hunt: pivot to termsrv.dll change, 'Apple Sync' task, and outbound SSH to the OkoBot bot IPs from the same host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("net.exe","net1.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop Users" and ProcessCommandLine has "add")
    or (FileName =~ "netsh.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "advfirewall" and ProcessCommandLine has "3389")
    or (FileName =~ "reg.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "fDenyTSConnections")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("net.exe","net1.exe") and CommandLine has "Remote Desktop Users" and CommandLine has "add")
    or (NewProcessName has "netsh.exe" and CommandLine has "advfirewall" and CommandLine has "3389")
    or (NewProcessName has "reg.exe" and CommandLine has "fDenyTSConnections")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 ((@Image:(*\net.exe OR *\net1.exe OR *\NET.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*Remote?Desktop?Users* AND @CommandLine:*add*) OR (@Image:(*\netsh.exe OR *\NETSH.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*advfirewall* AND @CommandLine:*3389*) OR (@Image:(*\reg.exe OR *\REG.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*fDenyTSConnections*))

| ((ImageFileName=/net1?\.exe$/i CommandLine=/Remote Desktop Users/i CommandLine=/add/i) OR (ImageFileName=/netsh\.exe$/i CommandLine=/advfirewall/i CommandLine=/3389/) OR (ImageFileName=/reg\.exe$/i CommandLine=/fDenyTSConnections/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name IN (net.exe,net1.exe) Processes.process="*Remote Desktop Users*" Processes.process="*add*") OR (Processes.process_name=netsh.exe Processes.process="*advfirewall*" Processes.process="*3389*") OR (Processes.process_name=reg.exe Processes.process="*fDenyTSConnections*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name IN (net.exe,net1.exe) Processes.process="*Remote Desktop Users*" Processes.process="*add*") OR (Processes.process_name=netsh.exe Processes.process="*advfirewall*" Processes.process="*3389*") OR (Processes.process_name=reg.exe Processes.process="*fDenyTSConnections*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Reverse SSH tunnel to OkoBot infrastructure from user endpoint AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the TookPS SSH tunnel: sshd.exe making outbound public connections (reverse tunnel) from a workstation, or ssh/sshd reaching OkoBot's confirmed bot IPs 104.243.43.16, 104.243.32.213, 62.210.188.209. SSH daemon egress from an endpoint is abnormal. Rationale: The three SSH-bot IPs are from Securelist's IOC list; sshd.exe egress is the reverse-tunnel behaviour the article describes (forwarding local RDP over SSH). Endpoint SSH daemon outbound is inherently rare. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/okobot-framework-targets-cryptocurrency-wallets/120660/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/okobot-malware-framework-injects-seed.html
ATT&CKT1572 T1071.001 T1090
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running an SSH reverse tunnel legitimately (e.g. remote dev access) — check user role
  • IT using OpenSSH server on a jump host
  • Automated backup/replication over SSH from a server (not a workstation)
  • CI runner establishing SSH to a build host
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process is sshd.exe (daemon egressing = tunnel) and resolve the remote IP; match against the three bot IPs. 2) Contain: kill ssh/sshd, delete %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\go.bat and the 'Apple Sync' task, block the IPs at egress, isolate host. 3) Hunt: enumerate other hosts beaconing to the same IPs and check for the RDP-enablement chain and OkoBot staging files.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sshd.exe" and RemoteIPType == "Public")
    or (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ssh.exe","sshd.exe") and RemoteIP in ("104.243.43.16","104.243.32.213","62.210.188.209"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("104.243.43.16","104.243.32.213","62.210.188.209")
    or (DstPortNumber == 22 and NetworkDirection =~ "Outbound")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@Image:(*\sshd.exe OR *\SSHD.EXE) OR @DestinationIp:(104.243.43.16 OR 104.243.32.213 OR 62.210.188.209))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4
| (ContextImageFileName=/sshd\.exe$/i OR RemoteAddressIP4=/^(104\.243\.43\.16|104\.243\.32\.213|62\.210\.188\.209)$/)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
